\paragraph{Matrix run settings.}
The matrix table is generated with one uniform benchmark setup. The full refresh command is:
\begin{lstlisting}[language=bash,breaklines=true,breakatwhitespace=true]
pyAmpliCol/dependencies/.venv/bin/python pyAmpliCol/docs/result_matrix.py --color-accuracy full --data /Users/vjhirsch/HEP_programs/pyAmpliCol/pyAmpliCol/docs/result_matrix_full_data.json --table /Users/vjhirsch/HEP_programs/pyAmpliCol/pyAmpliCol/docs/result_matrix_full_table.tex --generate-data 1-9 --show-data 1-9 --time-limit 900 --target-runtime 1 --amplicol-points 10000 --jobs 4 --n-cores 4 --process-workers 1 --columns-per-table 3
\end{lstlisting}
\noindent\footnotesize Partial refreshes use the same settings with \texttt{--base-process}, \texttt{--skip-jit}, \texttt{--skip-cpp-o3}, \texttt{--process-ids}, or \texttt{--skip-amplicol} added only to restrict which cells are updated.  PyAmpliCol-only refreshes may additionally use \texttt{--process-workers 5}; this is intentionally disabled when the \AC\ reference is refreshed because that path uses shared top-level generated-library files.  \AC\ reference timings for this colour table use the raw generated-library sequence \texttt{amplicol\_generate --library=create-raw}, \texttt{make -j4 amplicol\_generate\_library}, and the dedicated \texttt{amplicol\_color\_library\_probe}.  The raw library is created before LC helicity merging so that NLC/full colour-order interferences are preserved.  \PAC\ rows use the generic staged-DAG artifact, Rusticol double precision, JIT or C++ O3 Symbolica evaluators as labelled, and \texttt{time-process} with a one-second target runtime.  The \texttt{--time-limit} setting applies only to C++ O3 generation; \AC\ and JIT rows are left uncapped.
\par\smallskip
\paragraph{Fortran colour-reference limitations.}
The following cells are generated and evaluated by \PAC, but have no direct \AC\ NLC/full-colour matrix reference because the current Fortran \texttt{init\_col} reference path stops above two quark lines: $d\bar d\to u\bar{u}\,s\bar{s}+(n-4)g$, \(n=4\).  Their \PAC\ slots are shown as absolute timings.
\par\smallskip
\paragraph{C++ O3 compile-budget gaps.}
The following cells have validated \AC\ and \PAC\ JIT rows but no completed C++ O3 row; their C++ slot is a localized performance-generation compile-budget gap, not a physics-validation failure: $gg\to t\bar t+(n-2)g$, \(n=4\): timed out; $gg\to gg+(n-2)g$, \(n=4\): timed out.
\par\smallskip
